judgment.notes: M001 is instantiated with W=X, exponent a and set A. A metric space supplies the induced emetric structure, and X is explicitly equipped with its Borel measurable structure. M001 has no measurability or boundedness condition on A and no exponent restriction; the additional a>0 is retained for the content interpretation. D003 is used only after finite diameter establishes boundedness. There are no E applications.

S001 identifies admissible finite-scale covers and costs, preserves countable costs under empty padding, proves the infimum inequalities and scale monotonicity, and removes r=∞ by domination by any finite positive scale. Every other positive extended scale has a positive real representative, giving exactly the stated supremum. S002 uses the lower-bound property to obtain actual admissible covers and the upper-bound property to force content zero, treating ∞ and an empty admissible class correctly. S003 combines the supremum identity and F002 in both directions. No limit exchange or regularity hypothesis is needed.

The only direct premise used is M001. F001 is proved in S001 before its use in S002–S003; F002 is proved in S002 before its use in S003. Both retain L1. L2–L6 are discharged within their stated arguments, and L1 is discharged into a>0 at the end. Reindexed families depend only on the chosen countable cover; the small-cover witnesses depend on δ and ε as exported. All other factual uses are routine local facts justified in background_notes; no producer body, ambient H or future fact is needed.

The packet alone supplies the necessary content and diameter definitions, the full M001 equality and its conditions, the complete N001 statement and S001–S003. Replaying those steps with the positively checked routine background below yields every clause of N001. No original manuscript, other R proof, absent project lemma or expanded permission claim is used.

N001 quantifies X,A,a with a>0 and all positive scales/tolerances; its binder explicitly uses X's Borel structure. D002–D006 specify the diameter convention, cost, admissibility, extended codomain and Hausdorff normalization. The real-diameter notation is guarded by boundedness, established for each finite-scale member. Empty costs, countable reindexing, both infimum bounds, monotonicity and both zero criteria are exported explicitly, with no private local witness or unresolved identification.
